strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH#63275 / PR 66247: non-finite float inf/-inf and overflowing round float or int with coarse unit in Timedelta/to_timedelta raise bare OverflowError on buggy commit 20542d17b1cc instead of OutOfBoundsTimedelta (or NaT under errors=coerce). Build pandas from source at the buggy commit with no-build-isolation editable install, then run the two added test files' new tests, which should fail on buggy and pass on fixed.

pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era table entry; versions left unpinned and must be chosen at install time, so the environment is not pinned by evidence
Build must use --no-build-isolation so the Cython version installed in the environment is used to compile the extensions

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_constructors.py::TestTimedeltaConstructors -k 'float_inf_raises or round_float_overflow_unit' pandas/tests/tools/test_to_timedelta.py -k 'to_timedelta_object_inf or unit_non_round_floats' -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 20542d17b1cc the new tests fail: Timedelta(inf) and Timedelta(1e19, unit='s') raise bare OverflowError, which pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match='without overflow') does not catch, so the test errors. On the fixed revision (PR 66247 applied) the same tests pass: OutOfBoundsTimedelta is raised with message containing 'without overflow', and to_timedelta(..., errors='coerce') returns NaT.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timedelta(float('inf')) and Timedelta(1e19, unit='s') on the buggy build: observe the exception type (OverflowError versus OutOfBoundsTimedelta).
risks: NaN never reaches the is_integer branch; the tests use only inf and -inf, so NaN is not a reproduction input
The np.timedelta64 OverflowError wrapping only applies when unit is not 'ns'; the round-float test uses unit='s' so it is in scope
The repo's test for to_timedelta_unit_non_round_floats is listed in -k only as a sanity selector; it is not part of the reproducing transition

The buggy commit's build depends on the unpinned NumPy and Cython chosen at install; a mismatched NumPy ABI could break compilation and be mistaken for a reproduction, so verify the build succeeds on buggy before reading test results
Evidence contains no platform or sanitiser requirement; the behaviour is a Python-level exception path, expected to be platform-independent on 64-bit Linux, but this is inferred, not stated
The PR date is blank in the context, so the exact era of dependency versions is unknown and cannot be inferred from the PR
The issue discussion is about dtype and unit-of-output choices and does not supply numerical expected values; expected behaviour rests on the PR body and the tests

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_constructors.py and pandas/tests/tools/test_to_timedelta.py in the PR diff
oracle.why: The defect is an exception-type transition, not a numeric value; the test asserts the exception class and message substring 'without overflow' and the NaT result under coerce, so the comparison is exact on those.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 20542d17b1cc, Timedelta(np.inf) calls int(item) in the float branch, which raises a bare OverflowError; pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta) does not match it, so the assertion errors and the test fails. Timedelta(1e19, unit='s') goes through np.timedelta64 and raises bare OverflowError, also failing the match.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision item.is_integer() returns False for inf, so the value falls to _numeric_to_td64ns, which raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta with 'without overflow'; to_timedelta(errors='coerce') returns NaT; the round-float overflow path raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta, so all assertions hold.
